nodes.description: KY associates with the BAG3/HSPB8 chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA) machinery that clears damaged filamin C; KY deficiency reduces basal autophagic flux, impairing that clearance. CASA factors (BAG3, HSPB8, filamin C) are transcriptionally upregulated in KY-deficient models as an early, apparently compensatory response.

evidence.reference_title: Myofibrillar myopathy-associated KY protein promotes muscle fibre size rescue independent of its predicted catalytic triad.
evidence.snippet: basal autophagic flux is significantly reduced in both KY-deficient C2C12 cells and ky/ky muscle fibres.

evidence.snippet: upregulation of CASA factors appears to be an early and primary molecular hallmark of KY deficiency.

nodes.description: Progressive multiple joint contractures (neck, elbows, hips, feet, and other joints).

evidence.snippet: Mutations in KY cause Myofibrillar Myopathy-7 (MFM-7) and Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (HSP).

nodes.description: KY is transcribed in central nervous system tissues, and its loss is proposed to impair upper-motor-neuron / corticospinal function, explaining the spastic-paraplegia presentation seen in one kindred. This CNS role is hypothesized, not demonstrated (see mechanistic_hypotheses).

evidence.reference_title: Progressive hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by a homozygous KY mutation.
evidence.snippet: KY transcription in CNS tissues may imply that it also has a role in neuromotor function, in line with the irregularity of neuromuscular junction in Ky null mutant mice.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in KY abolish or severely reduce kyphoscoliosis peptidase, a transglutaminase-like Z-disc protein. Although it carries a predicted catalytic triad, recombinant KY shows no detectable enzymatic activity and the catalytic residues are dispensable for its muscle-fiber-size function; its demonstrated role is binding its partner filamin C at the Z-disc, and that scaffolding function is lost.

evidence.reference_title: A new early-onset neuromuscular disorder associated with kyphoscoliosis peptidase (KY) deficiency.
evidence.snippet: We describe a new early-onset neuromuscular disorder due to a homozygous loss-of-function variant in the kyphoscoliosis peptidase gene (KY).

evidence.reference_title: Myofibrillar myopathy-associated KY protein promotes muscle fibre size rescue independent of its predicted catalytic triad.
evidence.snippet: replacements of the predicted catalytic residues do not impair the protein's ability to rescue fibre size in ky/ky muscle, indicating that the predicted catalytic residues are dispensable for fibre size rescue in these assays.
